Account background: Boreal Sprint Labs (productivity SaaS for field teams). ~450 employees, HQ in Seattle. CTO Mark Liu leading infra decisions; Head of Product (Sara Kim) owns integration success. Use-case: in-app recommendations + real-time support agent augmentation + nightly reranking of event logs for insights. Primary constraint: must isolate PII-containing signals in VPC; SOC2 and KMS required for keys.

Sales/technical history (shorthand):
- 2024-09-12: initial intro (Alex) — interest in hosted API to speed POC.
- 2024-09-18: demo (Priya) — Redwood hosted flows, streaming, embeddings demoed. CTO asked about latency @ 95th percentile.
- 2024-09-20: hosted API POC started (fireflies ff_20240920_boreal_poc). Small workload: chat+embeddings.
- 2024-10-02: hosted POC metrics: stable, avg latencies 80-110ms for short prompts; cost baseline established. Team asked about dedicated for predictable peak loads (weekly batch + spike events).
- 2024-10-10: technical deep-dive (Priya + infra) — discussed prefix caching, batching knobs, model quantization guidance.
- 2024-10-18: Dedicated POC requested. Redwood provisioned 2-slot dedicated pool equivalent (customer notes: 2 x A10G-like slots) for 2-week stress test.
- 2024-10-25: Dedicated POC mid-review (ff_20241028_pricing_call) — measured sustained throughput 750 reqs/min, 95p latency 120ms under normal batching. Spike test: 2.5x traffic causes 95p to approach 220ms without burst capacity.
- 2024-10-28: pricing conversation started (pricing deck v3). Finance asks for committed model and ramp schedule options.
- 2024-11-01: security questionnaire submitted; awaiting answers on KMS/HSM integration and audit log retention.

POC takeaways / decision criteria (customer language paraphrased):
- "We need predictable latency during event spikes; can't re-architect client side to tolerate long tail delays." — Mark Liu
- Required latency SLO: 95th <= 150ms for chat routes; tokenization/embeddings can be looser.
- Throughput target: baseline 600-800 reqs/min with 3x headroom for marketing events.
- Cost sensitivity: want unit economics better than hosted pay-as-you-go at scale; committed pricing must show clear savings by month 3.
- Model compatibility: prefer open/Redwood-verified models (Llama-family & select curated variants); must support quantized weights and kernel selection.

Pricing & packaging positions discussed (negotiation notes):
- Redwood proposed committed dedicated tier options (examples):
  * Option A - Entry commit: 2 dedicated slots (A10G-equivalent) at $25,000/month base; burst to 4 slots available for 60 minutes/day at no extra charge for first 30 days of ramp; overage billed at 1.6x baseline rate beyond burst.
  * Option B - Ramp commit: 1.25x month1 credit, 1.5x month2 credit, full 2-slot month3 commit; $20k/month effective first two months (ramp credits applied) then $25k.
  * Option C - Higher commit: 4 slots reserved at $45,000/month with lower per-overage multiplier (1.25x) and included 2x burst cap (for predictable spikes).
- Customer asks: additive burst policy vs. metered overage? Wants clear daily burst budget and an explicit overage cap to avoid surprise bills.
- Overage math: customer wants to see worked example for 3 typical traffic patterns (steady, weekly spike, marketing flash sale).
- Billback model: prefer single monthly invoice with committed discount applied, detailed token/slot usage breakdown for internal chargeback.

Technical commercial asks from Boreal:
- Include 90-day ramp schedule: 50% commit credit month1, 75% month2, 100% month3 (finance-friendly).
- 30-days free burst credits during ramp (to prove safety).
- Clear SLA for failover: automatic fallback to hosted API in case Dedicated pool issues; define RTO and cost treatment during fallback.
- KMS integration details + audit logging retention (12 months min).

Open risks / blockers:
- Security needs written KMS/HSM integration plan and SOC2 artifact (infosec needs it before final sign-off).
- Legal wants MSA/SOW language on overage caps and termination for convenience with ramp refunds clarified.
- Finance needs clear ARR schedule and PO lead time; weekly forecast updates requested.
